decision.summary: The Fed held its policy rate at 0% to 0.25%. The vote was 11-1. Dissenting: Jeffrey M. Lacker.

changes.quote: Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in October suggests that economic activity and employment have continued to expand at a moderate pace in recent months, apart from weather-related disruptions.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Information received since the Federal Open Market Committee met in September suggests that economic activity has continued to expand at a moderate pace in rece…”

changes.quote: Although the unemployment rate has declined somewhat since the summer, it remains elevated.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Growth in employment has been slow, and the unemployment rate remains elevated.”

changes.quote: Household spending has continued to advance, and the housing sector has shown further signs of improvement, but growth in business fixed investment has slowed.
changes.explanation: Reworded from the previous statement: “Household spending has advanced a bit more quickly, but growth in business fixed investment has slowed.”

changes.quote: Inflation has been running somewhat below the Committee’s longer-run objective, apart from temporary variations that largely reflect fluctuations in energy prices.
changes.explanation: New language added in this statement.

changes.quote: The housing sector has shown some further signs of improvement, albeit from a depressed level.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

changes.quote: Inflation recently picked up somewhat, reflecting higher energy prices.
changes.explanation: Language from the previous statement that was dropped.

tone_quotes.quote: Furthermore, strains in global financial markets continue to pose significant downside risks to the economic outlook.

In particular, the Committee decided to keep the target range for the federal funds rate at 0 to 1/4 percent and currently anticipates that this exceptionally low range for the federal funds rate will be appropriate at least as long as the unemployment rate remains above 6-1/2 percent, inflation between one and two years ahead is projected to be no more than a half percentage point above the Committee’s 2 percent longer-run goal, and longer-term inflation expectations continue to be well anchored.

The Committee also will purchase longer-term Treasury securities after its program to extend the average maturity of its holdings of Treasury securities is completed at the end of the year, initially at a pace of $45 billion per month.

for_you.text: Card rates should not move on this decision; a $5,000 balance at about 11.95% APR costs about $49.79 a month in interest.

Mortgages track the 10-year Treasury yield, not the fed funds rate. The 10-year was 1.72% and moved +6 bp on the day; if that move passed through, the payment on a new $300,000 30-year loan at 3.32% would rise by about $9.95 a month.
Savings yields should stay roughly where they are, since the Fed held rates.
Unemployment was 7.7%, and employers added an average of 162k jobs a month over the prior 3 months.

for_country.text: CPI inflation was 1.8% over the past year (November 2012); core PCE inflation, the Fed's preferred gauge, was 1.8%, against a 2% goal.
Real GDP grew at a 0.6% annualized pace in the latest reported quarter.
The 2-year Treasury yield, the most Fed-sensitive market rate, moved +1 bp on the day.
The broad trade-weighted dollar moved -0.08% on the day.

whats_next: The dictionary tone reading is dovish (leaning toward lower rates). The forecast model gave the next meeting: hold 86%, cut 11%, hike 3%.
